Added a second commit that consolidates the updater slice while it is under change:

- `install()` is now one composed method. The platform installs the staged package, so the version plumbing through `restartWithLatest`/`startInstalling`/`restartWithUpdate`/`prepareAndRestart` was ceremony and is gone.
- `check()` now dispatches to two linear flows: `findAndStage()` (visible, the normal path) and `refreshStaged()` (silent). No more interleaved `if (!staged)` branches.
- The `enabled` flag is removed; platform presence is enablement, so an enabled controller without a platform is unrepresentable.
- `showUpdaterDialog` loses `alertOnFail` (every caller passed `true`); the unused `downloading.percent` field is deleted.
- `updater-ipc.ts` and the shallow `updater-subscriptions` module fold into `updater.ts`. The slice is now three files: shell, state machine, adapter.

Net -50 lines. Behavior is unchanged; all 12 controller tests pass, and `bun typecheck` passes in `packages/desktop` and `packages/app`.
Thanks for updating your PR! It now meets our contributing guidelines. :+1:

Additional confirmed reproduction + evidence from a real install (Windows, opencode desktop bundle + CLI):

1. **Wrap point measured precisely**: the 6-byte field rolls over at `2026-08-14 11:23:02 UTC` on this machine. A message at `08-13 15:28 UTC` gets ID prefix `FFBBCCE2D000` (`msg_ffbbcce2d001uUMvHYqYBDb6Cp`) while messages a few hours later start with `000E...`/`0039...`. So `latest()` picks the stale `ffb...` assistant as the "latest".

2. **Concrete sorted-vs-time mismatch** in the affected session:
   - chronologically last message: `msg_003a81e41001ylDQOsSbNrB8ZX` (user)
   - lexicographically max message: `msg_ffbbcce2d001uUMvHYqYBDb6Cp` (assistant, `finish=stop`)
   → loop condition `lastUser.id < lastAssistant.id` is true and the loop `break`s with only `loop step=0 -> exiting loop` in the log; no `process`/`stream` ever runs.

3. **Affects any session spanning the wrap point, regardless of model/provider**. In our case the stuck session had messages with 4 different models (deepseek-v4-flash-free, qwen, minimax, local) - all silently dropped. Confirms it is not provider/model related.

4. **CLI reproduces it too** (not desktop-UI only): `opencode run --session <id> ... --print-logs` on the same DB logs `loop step=0` then `exiting loop` immediately.

5. **Workaround for users until merged**: sessions created entirely after the wrap time (all IDs monotonic) keep working; for stuck sessions, `--fork` into a new session works.

FWIW the bundled desktop code path is `latest()` selecting by `info.id > user.id` (string compare) in `packages/opencode/src/session/message-v2.ts`, exactly as described. The proposed fix (order by `time.created` with id tiebreaker) is correct; `id.ts` should also keep more than 6 bytes (or use a proper monotonic ULID) so IDs stay sortable across wraps.

I reproduced this failure family in a real session without custom message IDs or clock skew.

OpenCode's own ascending ID generator wraps its effective millisecond timestamp every `2^36` ms (about 795.36 days): it multiplies `Date.now()` by `0x1000`, then stores six bytes. On OpenCode 1.18.4, the boundary occurred at `2026-08-14T11:19:55.136Z`.

A session's last completed turn had `msg_fff...` IDs; its next user messages had `msg_002...` IDs. The messages were persisted, but `MessageV2.latest()` selected the lexicographically greatest old user, and `runLoop()` exited on that old completed user/assistant pair. No assistant child was created for the chronologically latest user, so the visible symptom was a silent non-response.

A read-only audit found 209 of 244 Discord-mapped historical sessions would have ignored a newly generated message under 1.18.4 at the time of testing. This is related to #18807, but the trigger here is the deterministic internal timestamp wrap rather than two clocks.

The released v1.18.18 source appears to contain both necessary fixes:

- `latest()` compares `time.created`, using ID only as a tie-breaker.
- Loop completion checks `lastAssistant.parentID === lastUser.id`.

A useful regression test would generate messages immediately before and after a `2^36` ms boundary and assert that the post-wrap user is selected and receives an assistant child.

> ### Fix
> Set the User-Agent directly on your request:`opencode`
> 
> curl -s https://opencode.ai \
>   -H "Authorization: Bearer <key-or-public>" \
>   -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
>   -H "User-Agent: opencode/1.18.16" \
>   -d '{"model":"deepseek-v4-flash-free","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"hi"}],"max_tokens":5}'
> **Verified:** Including the UA returns an HTTP 200 (including streaming). Excluding it results in a 429 error, regardless of IP or key.`opencode/`
>

> [@cubelitblade](https://github.com/cubelitblade)
> 
> ### Root Cause
> The issue is triggered by the **`User-Agent` header**, not the API key or IP address. The upstream "Console" inference provider (which serves the `-free` models) gates anonymous free capacity strictly based on this header:
> 
> * **TUI request** (`User-Agent: opencode/<version>`) →  `200 OK`
> * **Custom request** (`User-Agent: curl/8.0` or any non-opencode UA) → `429 FreeUsageLimitError`
> 
> Testing confirmed that `x-opencode-client`, `x-opencode-version`, and session headers alone do not unlock the capacity. Only the `User-Agent` value matters.
> 
> According to the source code (`packages/opencode/src/session/llm/request.ts`), the TUI always sends `User-Agent: opencode/<version>`. The gateway strips all `x-opencode-*` headers before forwarding upstream but passes the `User-Agent` through untouched, allowing the upstream provider to use it for free-pool validation.
> 
> ### Fix
> Set the `opencode` User-Agent directly on your request:
> 
> curl -s https://opencode.ai \
>   -H "Authorization: Bearer <key-or-public>" \
>   -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
>   -H "User-Agent: opencode/1.18.16" \
>   -d '{"model":"deepseek-v4-flash-free","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"hi"}],"max_tokens":5}'
> **Verified:** Including the `opencode/` UA returns an HTTP 200 (including streaming). Excluding it results in a 429 error, regardless of IP or key.
> 
> ### Notes
> * This restriction **only affects `-free` models**. Paid and balance-backed models are not gated by the User-Agent.
> * This is an anti-abuse gate designed to reserve free capacity for the official client. Because of this, it **may change at any time**. For long-term stability, it is better to Bring Your Own Key (BYOK) with a non-free model.
> * If you are writing a custom client, inject `User-Agent: opencode/<version>` into the request. Please also forward the user's real IP so per-IP quotas remain fair.
> * The solution i make is this simple proxy https://github.com/12errh/zen-proxy it just change the agent header line so it can work.
